parallel.requirements: Reimplement gomplate from observed executable behavior and bundled documentation only, without source lookup, wrapping, downloading, or disallowed binary analysis.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Created task list, then delegated a 20-area behavioral probe workflow and a later five-library format implementation workflow while the parent retained global assembly responsibility.
parallel.implementation: Produced partial Go packages and support files, including CLI/config/math/net/YAML-format work and one JSONPath file write from a child, but delegated implementation work did not finish as a coherent returned set.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Packaged a final tree, but artifact validation was not ok and the major workflow results were null at closure, leaving no completed returned components to integrate cleanly.
parallel.verification: Some children ran probes and local package tests, but whole-solution verification ended only with the official compile_failed evaluation and no tests run.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Both workflows were killed with null results; many probe children were retried or still in progress and all five implementation children were still in progress when the run closed.

serial.requirements: Worked from the same cleanroom prompt, docs, and normal execution probes of the provided binary without delegation or external source access.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Used a single-agent implementation plan that created the Go module, build script, and internal packages, preserving one owner for probing, coding, and packaging.
serial.implementation: Built a broader local tree with `compile.sh`, `go.mod`, YAML parser files, and multiple packages such as funcs, datasource, render, config, flags, csv, math, and net.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Artifact packaging was ok and included the build script and package directories, though the final official evaluation still failed to compile.
serial.verification: Ran documentation reads, many executable probes, and local implementation edits; the official evaluator reported compile_failed with all tests not run.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Timed out before producing a compiling solution, but without child workflow loss or parallel coordination failures.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Recognized the cleanroom gomplate reimplementation task, the ban on source lookup and binary analysis, and the need to infer behavior from executable runs and bundled docs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Recognized the same cleanroom reverse-engineering prompt and worked from documentation plus normal CLI probes of the provided executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement disagreement is visible; the major difference is execution strategy and closure rather than understanding of the benchmark rules.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Decomposed behavior discovery into twenty namespace/CLI areas and then delegated five complex format libraries to implementation agents.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Used a single local owner to create the module, package directories, and build script, then proceeded package by package in one workspace context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel assigned far broader concurrent ownership and carried many live children; serial had one continuous implementer responsible for the tree and build path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Probe children were told to write detailed specs to `/tmp/spec`, and implementation children were told to stay in assigned directories with only standard-library dependencies.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run retained one local context while reading docs, probing the executable, and editing the implementation tree.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel context transfer depended on child-written specs and workflow aggregation; serial did not need cross-agent handoffs, though no specific missing brief or conflicting contract is proven.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Implemented pieces across scattered packages including JSONPath, YAML formatting, config, CLI, math, and net, but the implementation workflow remained in progress when killed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Created a Go module with `compile.sh` and many internal packages, including YAML parser files and package directories under `internal`.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial produced a more coherent buildable artifact structure, while parallel had partial component work and no completed implementation workflow return to consolidate.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Both delegated workflows ended with `status` killed and `result` null, so the parent did not receive completed aggregate findings or implementation results.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results to join; all observations and edits stayed in the main serial trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a result lifecycle bottleneck at workflow completion, whereas serial avoided that class of handoff and join dependency.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel shared-workspace work yielded a partial final artifact with internal packages and docs, but artifact validation marked the submission not ok.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial artifact validation marked the submitted tree ok and included `compile.sh`, `go.mod`, and internal package directories.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial packaging was more orderly, while parallel did not close the shared final tree cleanly; the evidence does not prove a concrete concurrent overwrite collision.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The official evaluator completed but reported `compile_failed`, leaving all 3538 tests not run.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The official evaluator also completed with `compile_failed` and all 3538 tests not run despite the serial artifact packaging being ok.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no official outcome split: both solutions failed before tests ran, so verification evidence supports `both_fail` rather than a discordant explanation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent spent the 2399-second agent budget while two workflows accumulated 25 total child slots, retries, over 2.7 million child tokens, and killed terminal state.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run also hit the 2399-second process timeout, but with no delegation and only 43 tool calls in a single-agent implementation loop.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both timed out, but parallel consumed closure time in broad workflow fan-out and retries; serial spent its budget directly on implementation and probing.

outcome_analysis.explanation: This is not a discordant official outcome: both completed evaluations failed with compile_failed and 0 of 3538 tests passed. The parallel attempt differed by spending much of the same fixed window in broad workflow fan-out and retries, producing killed workflows and null aggregate results; the serial attempt kept one local implementation path and packaged a more coherent tree but still failed to compile.
parallel_contributors: Broad 20-area probe fan-out and later five-library implementation fan-out consumed time and tokens before integration closure.
Both workflow states ended killed with null results, so delegated findings and implementation components were not returned as completed aggregate outputs.
serial_contributors: Serial used no delegation and kept probing, implementation, and packaging in one trajectory.
Serial artifact validation was ok and included compile.sh and package directories, but the code still did not compile under the official evaluator.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both attempts had ordinary implementation incompleteness severe enough to produce compile_failed.
Serial wrote a larger coherent internal package tree, while parallel left several delegated format libraries unfinished.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No outcome difference; retained pattern explains a realized parallel process consequence but not a discordant pass/fail result.

candidates.reason: Rejected: implementation was owned by the parent and later by the five format-library children, so the problem is not absence of an implementer.
Rejected: integration remained unfinished, but the parent/orchestrator retained global integration responsibility and no completed incompatible components required ownerless reconciliation.
Rejected: the parent created and packaged a final tree; failure reflects incomplete closure, not a missing designated assembly owner.
Rejected: the parent explicitly managed tasks and workflow stages, so no end-to-end pipeline owner was absent.
Rejected: no single mandatory serial preflight blocked the workers; the probe work was broad concurrent fan-out.
Rejected: investigation was not merely sequential before implementation because the parent also launched concurrent implementation while probes were unresolved.
Rejected: indispensable integration was starved, but the more specific evidence is collective fan-out and retries exhausting the budget.

The parent launched a 20-area probe workflow and then a five-library implementation workflow. The first workflow records repeated stalled-agent retries, high aggregate token and tool counts, killed status, and a null result; the second also ended killed with every implementation child still in progress. That collective breadth consumed the finite run window and displaced integration and build closure, while the serial control used one local implementation path and produced a packaged tree.
candidates.realized_consequence: The parallel run spent the deadline across broad child probing, retries, and five implementation children, leaving both workflow aggregate results null and the final artifact not compile-ready.
candidates.near_match_reason: Active children were interrupted by run closure, but the directly correctable boundary is the overbroad concurrent allocation and retry budget drain that produced those terminations.
